name: Soft Furnishing
tagline: Curtains, blinds, upholstery and rugs — the layer that finishes a room
description: Soft furnishing is the last 10% of the budget that does 40% of the work: it controls light, absorbs sound and adds the colour hard finishes cannot. Fabrics are specified by width, rub count and light behaviour, not just by pattern.

materials.name: Curtains
materials.blurb: Sheer, dim-out or blackout drapery on track or rod
materials.description: Fullness is what makes curtains look expensive — 2 to 2.5 times the track width, always. Layer a sheer with a dim-out so the room works at noon and at midnight.

materials.name: Roller blind
materials.blurb: Single fabric roll — the tidiest window covering there is
materials.description: Minimal stack, minimal cost, minimal fuss. Choose the openness factor deliberately: 1% blocks the view and the glare, 5% keeps the view and lets some glare through.

materials.name: Roman blind
materials.blurb: Fabric that folds into soft horizontal pleats
materials.description: Gives the softness of a curtain with the tidiness of a blind — good where a full drape would crowd the room. Needs a lining and enough headroom for the stack.

materials.name: Wooden blind
materials.blurb: Timber or faux-wood slats that shape the light
materials.description: Tilting slats give precise control over light and privacy at the same time, and the timber warms a room. Use faux-wood in bathrooms and kitchens where real timber would warp.

materials.name: Zebra / dual-shade blind
materials.blurb: Alternating sheer and solid bands that align or offset
materials.description: Sliding the bands into alignment lets light through; offsetting them blocks it. A single blind that does two jobs, which suits living rooms that face the street.

materials.name: Upholstery fabric
materials.blurb: Specified by rub count — the number that predicts wear
materials.description: Martindale rub count is the specification that matters: 15,000+ for domestic use, 30,000+ for commercial. Pattern is a preference; rub count is a performance requirement.

materials.name: Sofa fabric
materials.blurb: Heavy-duty weaves built for daily sitting
materials.description: The upholstery grade that takes the most punishment. Performance weaves now handle pets, children and food without looking technical — worth the premium on a family sofa.

materials.name: Cushions
materials.blurb: The cheapest way to change a room's palette
materials.description: Mix sizes and textures rather than matching a set — 60 cm at the back, 45 cm in front, one lumbar. Feather inserts sit properly; foam ones look stiff in photographs and in life.

materials.name: Rugs
materials.blurb: Hand-knotted, tufted or flat-weave — sized to the furniture
materials.description: The rug should be large enough for at least the front legs of every seat to sit on it; anything smaller makes the room look mean. Hand-knotted lasts generations, tufted lasts years.

specs.Sizing: Front legs of all seating on rug

materials.name: Carpets (wall to wall)
materials.blurb: Full-floor carpet for warmth and quiet
materials.description: Still the best acoustic floor available and the softest underfoot. Specify the pile weight and an anti-microbial treatment, and be honest with the client about cleaning in Indian dust.

materials.name: Bed linen
materials.blurb: Sheets, duvets and covers — specified by thread count and weave
materials.description: Percale for a crisp, cool hand and sateen for a silky one; 300–500 thread count in long-staple cotton is the sweet spot. Above that, the number is usually marketing.
